title: Term 3 and 4 Examination
instructions: This paper covers the work of Terms 3 and 4.
This question paper consists of 7 questions. Answer ALL the questions.
Read each question carefully before you answer it.
Show your working, and round your answers as each question asks.

questions.prompt: What is the SI unit of force?
Calculate the weight on Earth of a 45 kg learner. Use g = 10 N/kg.
An object's mass is smaller on the moon than on Earth.
questions.explanation: Mass stays the same; only weight changes.

questions.prompt: A trolley is pulled to the left with 80 N, while friction of 20 N acts to the right. What is the size of the resultant force?
A car moves at a constant speed in a straight line. The forces on it are…
options: zero because nothing acts on it

questions.prompt: Match each example to whether it increases or reduces friction.

pairs.left: Streamlined shape of a racing car

questions.prompt: A space probe far from any planet has its engines switched off. Describe and explain its motion.
questions.memo:
✓ It keeps moving at the same speed in the same direction (1)
✓ because there is no friction or air resistance, so no resultant force acts on it (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 2: Electric Cells, Resistance and Circuits

questions.prompt: An electric cell converts…
options: chemical potential energy into electrical energy

questions.prompt: Is a voltmeter connected in series or in parallel with a component?
What is the unit of resistance?
A thin wire has a lower resistance than a thick wire of the same material and length.
In a parallel circuit, branch currents are 0,4 A and 0,8 A. What is the total current from the battery?
Match each change to its effect on the resistance of a wire.

pairs.left: Replace a copper wire with a nichrome wire of the same size

questions.prompt: Why is nichrome used for the heating element in a kettle while copper is used for the cable?
questions.memo:
✓ Nichrome has high resistance, so it converts electrical energy into heat (1)
✓ Copper has low resistance, so very little energy is wasted in the cable (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 4: The Earth as a System

questions.prompt: Which sphere includes all the water on Earth?
Soil and rocks belong to the…
Why is the inner core solid even though it is extremely hot?
options: It is cooled by the mantle

questions.prompt: What type of rock is granite?
Fossils are mainly found in sedimentary rocks.
Match each metamorphic rock to the rock it formed from.
Explain why granite has large crystals but basalt has small crystals.
questions.memo:
✓ Granite forms from magma cooling slowly underground, giving crystals time to grow (1)
✓ Basalt forms from lava cooling quickly at the surface, so crystals stay small (1)

questions.prompt: Minerals are renewable resources.
Platinum is mainly used in…
The Big Hole in Kimberley is an example of…
In which province is most of South Africa's coal mined?
Match each mineral to the place where it is mainly mined.
Describe how mined land can be rehabilitated.
questions.memo: Any two (1 each): fill in pits and level the land; replace topsoil; replant indigenous plants; clean up waste dumps and treat polluted water

questions.prompt: Name the steps, in order, by which a metal is obtained from its ore.
questions.memo:
✓ Extraction/mining (1)
✓ Crushing and separating the mineral from waste rock (1)
✓ Refining/smelting to purify the metal (1)

questions.prompt: About what percentage of the air is oxygen?
In which layer of the atmosphere does weather occur?
In which layer is the ozone layer found?
Without any greenhouse effect, the Earth would be too cold for most life.
Match each layer to its feature.
Explain how the greenhouse effect warms the Earth.
questions.memo:
✓ The sun's energy passes through the atmosphere and heats the surface (1)
✓ The surface gives off heat (infrared radiation) (1)
✓ Greenhouse gases absorb this heat and re-radiate it back to Earth (1)

sections.title: QUESTION 7: Birth, Life and Death of Stars

questions.prompt: What is the name for a cloud of gas and dust in which stars are born?
In nuclear fusion in a main sequence star…
options: hydrogen nuclei join to form helium

questions.prompt: Name the two forces that are balanced in a main sequence star.
questions.memo:
✓ Gravity pulling inwards (1)
✓ Outward pressure from the energy released by fusion (1)

questions.prompt: Massive stars live longer than small stars.
questions.explanation: Massive stars use their fuel much faster, so they have shorter lives.
